dataset_name: Olist multi-table set (olist_orders_dataset.csv, olist_order_items_dataset.csv, olist_order_payments_dataset.csv, olist_customers_dataset.csv, olist_products_dataset.csv, olist_sellers_dataset.csv, olist_geolocation_dataset.csv, olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv, product_category_name_translation.csv)
recommended_ingestion_source: generic_csv, via app/services/ecommerce_olist_adapter.py::flatten_olist_dataset() + ingest_olist_dataset() -- NOT via any HTTP route or Celery task, since none exists to invoke this adapter (confirmed, see 01_dataset_discovery.json).
summary: A real, well-formed, referentially-clean multi-table relational dataset. An adapter (ecommerce_olist_adapter.py) already exists in the repository and correctly joins orders+order_items+payments into GENERIC_COLUMN_MAP's shape -- this is a purpose-built solution, not something this QA prompt needs to invent. However, the adapter is unwired to any route/task, and it discards Olist's real order_status column entirely, which would silently mislabel 2.98% of orders as 'fulfilled' regardless of their true status if this adapter were ever invoked.

olist_assessment.joins_required: Yes -- 3 tables minimum for the adapter's own scope: olist_orders_dataset.csv (order_date), olist_order_items_dataset.csv (line items, the join anchor), olist_order_payments_dataset.csv (payment method as channel stand-in). olist_customers_dataset.csv/olist_products_dataset.csv/olist_sellers_dataset.csv/olist_geolocation_dataset.csv/olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv/product_category_name_translation.csv are NOT joined by the existing adapter at all -- confirmed by reading ecommerce_olist_adapter.py in full, it only imports/merges orders_df, order_items_df, payments_df.
olist_assessment.how_tables_relate: order_items.order_id -> orders.order_id (many-to-one: 112,650 item rows across 98,666 distinct orders -- 9,803 orders have 2+ items). order_items.product_id -> products.product_id (many-to-one, 0 orphans). payments.order_id -> orders.order_id (many-to-one: 103,886 payment rows, 2,961 orders have 2+ payment rows e.g. split/installment payments). orders.customer_id -> customers.customer_id (0 orphans). All foreign-key relationships confirmed referentially intact via direct pandas isin() checks: 0 orphan order_items with no parent order, 0 orphan payments with no parent order, 0 orphan order_items with no matching product, 0 orphan orders with no matching customer.
olist_assessment.does_current_ingestion_support_multi_tab: No -- app/services/ecommerce_ingestion.py's own functions (extract_canonical_rows, ingest_dataframe) only ever accept a single pd.DataFrame. Multi-table support exists exclusively in the separate ecommerce_olist_adapter.py module, which pre-flattens before calling the same single-dataframe ingest_dataframe().
olist_assessment.does_an_adapter_already_exist: Yes -- app/services/ecommerce_olist_adapter.py::flatten_olist_dataset()/ingest_olist_dataset(), confirmed present and readable in full. This directly supersedes Scanwick_QA_Testing_Scripts.md's 2026-07-07 note that no such map/adapter exists yet for Olist -- that note is stale relative to the current repository.
olist_assessment.does_a_flattening_pipeline_already_exist: Yes, same file -- flatten_olist_dataset() merges order_items+orders+primary-payment-method into one dataframe shaped exactly to GENERIC_COLUMN_MAP's expected columns (order_id, order_date, gross_revenue, currency, shipping_cost, channel, sku, quantity, unit_price).
olist_assessment.preprocessing_required: None beyond what the adapter already does -- flatten_olist_dataset() is a complete, self-contained preprocessing step (pandas merge only, no external dependency). The only remaining gap is operational: nothing currently calls this function outside of its own tests.

field_mapping.evidence: flatten_olist_dataset(): 'order_id' = order_id + '-' + order_item_id (ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:56) -- a real Olist order spanning multiple items becomes multiple distinct canonical 'orders', same 1-item-per-order simplification already used for Shopify/WooCommerce.
ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:57, joined in from orders_df via order_id.

ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:58,64 -- both canonical fields are set to the same source value 'price', which is correct here since Olist's order_items.price is already a genuine per-unit-per-line-item figure (unlike the ecommerce_orders_10k_updated.csv finding above, this is NOT a mapping defect -- Olist's price column is legitimately both the line's revenue and its unit price, since quantity is fixed at 1 per row).

ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:59 -- hardcoded to 'BRL', Olist's real, documented currency (Brazilian e-commerce dataset) -- not a fabricated default, a correct constant for this dataset's real provenance.

ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:44-48,61 -- for orders with multiple payment rows (2,961 of them), only the first payment method (sorted by payment_sequential) is kept; any secondary/split payment method is dropped.
ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:62 -- Olist's product_id (an opaque catalog ID) is used directly as sku.

ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:63 -- hardcoded to 1 for every row. Confirmed accurate (not fabricated): Olist's order_items table is already one row per physical unit sold, so quantity=1 per row is a correct literal fact about the source data, not an assumption.

olist_products_dataset.csv has no cost/price field at all (only product_weight_g/product_length_cm/product_height_cm/product_width_cm and category/name-length metadata) -- there is no COGS data anywhere in the Olist set, so unit_cogs is never populated by design, not by omission. This will correctly trigger the 100%-COGS-missing disabled-feature rule if ingested.

Olist has no email field anywhere (only customer_zip_code_prefix/customer_city/customer_state) -- customer_email is never populated, so Order.customer_id will be None for every Olist order ingested via this adapter.

flatten_olist_dataset()'s output dataframe (ecommerce_olist_adapter.py:54-66) has no key carrying over order_status at all, and does not populate a 'refund_amount' key either. Consequently, if this adapter's output were ingested, _resolve_generic_status() (ecommerce_ingestion.py:163-170) would receive refund_amount=None for every row (unresolved, no fallback role exists for refund_amount) and therefore assign OrderStatus.fulfilled to every single Olist order, regardless of its real status. Quantified via direct inspection of the real orders_dataset.csv: 96,478 delivered (97.02%), 1,107 shipped, 625 canceled, 609 unavailable, 314 invoiced, 301 processing, 5 created, 2 approved -- 2,963 orders (2.98%) have a real non-delivered status that would be silently overwritten to 'fulfilled' if this adapter were actually used to ingest data.
These 5 files are not read by flatten_olist_dataset() at all -- confirmed by reading the adapter's full source; only orders_df, order_items_df, payments_df are accepted parameters.

data_quality.duplicate_order_ids: Not applicable to check pre-flattening in the same sense as a flat file -- order_id is a legitimate one-to-many parent key by design in a relational schema; post-flattening, the synthesized external_order_id (order_id+'-'+order_item_id) is unique by construction.
data_quality.malformed_prices: Not exhaustively checked in this pass beyond confirming order_items.price/freight_value are present with 0 nulls in the columns inspected -- a full numeric-range/negative-value sweep of Olist's own price/freight_value columns was not performed in this prompt and should be considered Not Observed rather than assumed clean.
data_quality.malformed_timestamps: olist_orders_dataset.csv has null order_approved_at (160 rows), order_delivered_carrier_date (1,783 rows), order_delivered_customer_date (2,965 rows) -- order_purchase_timestamp itself (the one actually used by the adapter for order_date) has 0 nulls.
data_quality.missing_sku: 0 -- product_id is populated for all 112,650 order_items rows (join to products.csv confirmed 0 orphans, implying product_id is always present and valid).
data_quality.missing_customer_ids: Structurally: Order.customer_id will be None for 100% of ingested rows (no email data exists in Olist at all) -- this is a permanent, by-design gap, not a per-row data-quality defect.
data_quality.missing_cogs: 100% -- no cost data exists anywhere in the Olist set.
data_quality.encoding_problems: None observed during pandas read of any of the 9 files.
data_quality.orphan_records: 0 across every foreign-key relationship checked (items->orders, payments->orders, items->products, orders->customers) -- this is a clean, well-formed relational dataset.
data_quality.unsupported_currencies: N/A -- currency is a fixed 'BRL' constant applied by the adapter, not read from source data (Olist itself has no currency column).
data_quality.inconsistent_channel_names: payment_type has a small, fixed vocabulary in real Olist data (not exhaustively enumerated in this pass) -- used as a channel stand-in, not a true sales-channel concept.
data_quality.invalid_return_data: N/A -- Olist has no returns concept in the 3 files the adapter reads; olist_order_reviews_dataset.csv exists but is unrelated to returns and is not read by the adapter at all.

verdict: PASS WITH ISSUES. The Olist set is real, clean, and referentially intact, and the repository already contains a correctly-scoped adapter to flatten it into the canonical ingestion path. Two things must be true for Prompt 2 to test this dataset: (1) it must be invoked via direct function calls (flatten_olist_dataset/ingest_olist_dataset), since no route or Celery task exposes it; (2) the order_status data-loss finding (2.98% of orders would be mislabeled 'fulfilled') should be treated as a known, pre-documented consequence of the adapter's current design, not a new bug to rediscover independently.
